posts.author_name: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
posts.text: One of the few general rules in ecology is that biodiversity increases as you approach the equator. But there’s an exception. The global latitudinal diversity gradient for birds is three times weaker in cities than in natural areas. In PNAS: https://ow.ly/9xmR50ZFVLZ

There are more than a billion #cattle worldwide. Adding #seaweed to cattle feed can significantly reduce #methane #emissions. How much of an impact could this approach have? In PNAS Front Matter: https://ow.ly/kWLl50ZFWgJ

posts.author_name: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
posts.text: A deep dive into the capacity for trees to physiologically adapt to drought reaches a sobering conclusion: Trees have little ability to change their inner hydraulic systems to accommodate increasing levels of drought as the climate changes. In PNAS: https://ow.ly/rcBR50ZFVIC

The past century has seen strong El Niño events happening more frequently than in the 1,000 years before human-generated greenhouse-gas emissions began to warm the planet

posts.external_title: Why are El Niños getting stronger? 1000-year-coral record points to climate change
posts.external_description: A reconstruction of Pacific Ocean sea surface temperatures adds to the evidence that human-caused warming is boosting El Niño events.
